chapter_text:
CHAPTER 3 — आरोग्यं परमं सुखम् (AROGYAM PARAMAM SUKHAM)

प्रस्तावना (Introduction)

The title of this chapter — आरोग्यं परमं सुखम् — means "health is the highest happiness". The word आरोग्यम् is built from अरोगः (a-rogah, "one who is free from disease": अ = not + रोगः = disease) with the abstract taddhita suffix ष्यञ्, giving the sense "the state of being free from disease" (रोगाभावः आरोग्यम्). Indian tradition has always counted health as the first wealth: without a healthy body (स्वस्थं शरीरम्) and a calm mind (शान्तं मनः), neither study (अध्ययनम्), nor work (कर्म), nor duty (धर्मः), nor happiness (सुखम्) is possible. In this lesson (NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit, Course 309) we read simple Sanskrit prose about दिनचर्या (the daily regimen), आहारः (diet), निद्रा (sleep), व्यायामः (exercise), स्वच्छता (cleanliness), ऋतुचर्या (the seasonal regimen) and मनःस्वास्थ्यम् (mental health), together with famous public-domain verses on health — each with शब्दार्थ (word meanings), अन्वय (prose order) and भाव (purport) — and we draw grammar (सन्धि, समास, विभक्ति, कृदन्त) from the same material. Note: everything here is general, traditional wisdom about a healthy lifestyle, not medical advice or treatment.

आरोग्यस्य महत्त्वम् (The importance of health)

श्लोकः 1 (परम्परागतम् सुभाषितम् — traditional maxim):
आरोग्यं परमं भाग्यं स्वास्थ्यं सर्वार्थसाधनम् ।
शब्दार्थ: आरोग्यम् = health, freedom from disease; परमम् = highest, supreme; भाग्यम् = fortune, blessing; स्वास्थ्यम् = well-being (स्व + स्थ — "being established in oneself"); सर्वार्थसाधनम् = the means (साधनम्) of accomplishing all (सर्व) aims (अर्थ).
Translation: Health is the highest fortune; well-being is the instrument for achieving every goal of life.
भाव: All achievement rests on health. A sick body can neither earn, nor learn, nor serve.

श्लोकः 2 (चरकसंहिता, सूत्रस्थानम् 1.15):
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् आरोग्यं मूलमुत्तमम् ।
रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः श्रेयसो जीवितस्य च ॥
शब्दार्थ: धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् = of धर्म (duty), अर्थ (wealth), काम (desire) and मोक्ष (liberation) — the four पुरुषार्थाः (aims of human life); आरोग्यम् = health; मूलम् = root, foundation; उत्तमम् = best, foremost; रोगाः = diseases; तस्य = of that (health); अपहर्तारः = takers-away, robbers; श्रेयसः = of welfare, of the good; जीवितस्य = of life; च = and.
अन्वय: आरोग्यं धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् उत्तमं मूलम् (अस्ति)। रोगाः तस्य (आरोग्यस्य), श्रेयसः जीवितस्य च अपहर्तारः (भवन्ति)।
Translation: Health is the best root of the four aims of life — duty, wealth, desire and liberation. Diseases are the robbers of that health, of welfare, and of life itself.
भाव: The ancient physician Charaka places health at the very foundation of all four पुरुषार्थs. Disease steals not only comfort but the very possibility of a good life.

श्लोकः 3 (कालिदासः, कुमारसम्भवम् 5.33 — एकः पादः):
शरीरमाद्यं खलु धर्मसाधनम् ।
शब्दार्थ: शरीरम् = the body; आद्यम् = the first, foremost; खलु = indeed, surely; धर्मसाधनम् = the instrument (साधनम्) of धर्म (duty, righteous action).
Translation: The body is indeed the first instrument of duty.
भाव: Kalidasa reminds us that even the loftiest spiritual or moral effort needs a healthy body as its tool. Caring for the body is therefore itself a part of धर्म, not vanity.

दिनचर्या (The daily regimen)

सरलः गद्यपाठः (simple Sanskrit prose):
आदर्शः छात्रः प्रातः ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते शय्यायाः उत्तिष्ठति। सः शौचं दन्तधावनं च करोति। ततः सः किञ्चित् व्यायामं योगासनं वा करोति। स्नात्वा सः प्रार्थनां करोति। ततः शान्तमनसा अध्ययनं करोति। सः समये मितं हितं च भोजनं भुङ्क्ते। दिवा सः विद्यालये पठति। सायं सः क्रीडाङ्गणे क्रीडति। रात्रौ सः समये शयनं करोति।
शब्दार्थ: ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते = in the brahma-muhurta, the auspicious period before sunrise; शय्यायाः = from the bed; उत्तिष्ठति = rises, gets up; शौचम् = bodily cleansing; दन्तधावनम् = cleaning of the teeth; योगासनम् = yoga posture; स्नात्वा = having bathed; प्रार्थनाम् = prayer; शान्तमनसा = with a calm mind; समये = at the proper time; मितम् = measured, moderate; हितम् = wholesome; भुङ्क्ते = eats; क्रीडाङ्गणे = on the playground; क्रीडति = plays; शयनम् = sleep, going to bed.
English: The ideal student rises from bed in the brahma-muhurta (before sunrise). He performs his ablutions and cleans his teeth. Then he does some exercise or yoga postures. Having bathed, he prays, and then studies with a calm mind. He eats moderate, wholesome food at the proper time. By day he studies at school; in the evening he plays on the playground; at night he goes to sleep at the proper time.
The word दिनचर्या means "the conduct (चर्या) of the day (दिनस्य)" — a regular, balanced order of daily activities. Rising early gives fresh air, quiet time for study, and an unhurried start; regularity in eating, working, playing and sleeping keeps both body and mind in rhythm.

आहारः मितभोजनं च (Diet and moderate eating)

तत्त्वानि (principles): (1) ताजं सरलं च भोजनम् — fresh, simple, home-style food; (2) ऋतु-अनुकूलानि फलानि शाकानि च — seasonal fruits and vegetables; (3) शनैः शनैः चर्वणम् — chewing slowly and well; (4) शुद्धं जलम् — clean water; (5) मितभोजनम् — eating in measured quantity, stopping a little before the stomach is full; (6) समये भोजनम् — eating at regular times.
A famous traditional maxim warns: अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम् — "when the earlier food is still undigested (अजीर्णे), eating (another meal) is poison (विषम्)". The self-controlled person of tradition is described as हितभुक् मितभुक् ऋतभुक् — one who eats what is wholesome (हितभुक्), eats in moderation (मितभुक्), and eats what is honestly earned (ऋतभुक्). The Charaka tradition likewise names three pillars (त्रयः उपस्तम्भाः) that hold up the house of health: आहारः (food), स्वप्नः (sleep) and ब्रह्मचर्यम् (disciplined living).

श्लोकः 4 (नीति-परम्परा — on avoiding excess):
अतिदानाद् बलिर्बद्धो ह्यतिमानात् सुयोधनः ।
अतिलौल्याद् रावणो हतः अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत् ॥
शब्दार्थ: अतिदानात् = through excessive giving; बलिः = King Bali; बद्धः = was bound; हि = indeed; अतिमानात् = through excessive pride; सुयोधनः = Suyodhana (Duryodhana); अतिलौल्यात् = through excessive greed/lust; रावणः = Ravana; हतः = was slain; अति = excess; सर्वत्र = everywhere, in everything; वर्जयेत् = one should avoid.
अन्वय: अतिदानात् बलिः बद्धः, अतिमानात् हि सुयोधनः (विनष्टः), अतिलौल्यात् रावणः हतः — (अतः) सर्वत्र अति वर्जयेत्।
Translation: Through excessive giving Bali was bound; through excessive pride Suyodhana (perished); through excessive greed Ravana was slain — therefore avoid excess in everything.
भाव: Even virtues become harmful in excess. Applied to health: excess in food, sleep, work, play or screen-time all damage आरोग्यम्. Moderation (मितता) is the golden rule.

निद्रा व्यायामः च (Sleep and exercise)

श्लोकः 5 (श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता 6.17):
युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु ।
युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
शब्दार्थ: युक्त = regulated, measured, disciplined; आहारविहारस्य = in food (आहार) and recreation (विहार); युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु = whose effort (चेष्टा) in actions (कर्मसु) is regulated; युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य = whose sleep (स्वप्न) and waking (अवबोध) are regulated; योगः = yoga, disciplined union/practice; भवति = becomes; दुःखहा = the destroyer (हा) of sorrow (दुःख).
अन्वय: युक्ताहारविहारस्य, कर्मसु युक्तचेष्टस्य, युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य (पुरुषस्य) योगः दुःखहा भवति।
Translation: For one whose food and recreation are regulated, whose effort in actions is regulated, and whose sleep and waking are regulated, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
भाव: The Gita's prescription for well-being is balance in four things — eating, recreation, work and sleep. Neither too much nor too little of any of them.
निद्रा: Timely, sufficient sleep repairs the body and refreshes the mind; late nights and irregular sleep dull memory and attention. समये शयनं समये उत्थानं च आरोग्यस्य रक्षकम् — sleeping and rising at regular times protects health.
व्यायामः: व्यायामेन शरीरं दृढं भवति, जाठराग्निः वर्धते, मनः च प्रसन्नं भवति — by exercise the body becomes firm, digestion strengthens, and the mind becomes cheerful. Walking (पादगमनम्), yoga postures (योगासनानि), outdoor games (क्रीडाः) and surya-namaskara are traditional, gentle forms of exercise; regularity matters more than intensity, and excess is to be avoided here too.

स्वच्छता ऋतुचर्या च (Cleanliness and the seasonal regimen)

स्वच्छता: Cleanliness is the visible half of health. भोजनात् पूर्वं हस्तौ प्रक्षालयेत् — one should wash the hands before eating; wear clean clothes (शुद्धवस्त्रम्); keep the home, school and surroundings clean (परिसरस्वच्छता); keep food and water covered. Much disease travels through unclean hands, water and surroundings, so स्वच्छता is disease-prevention in daily action — as the saying goes, स्वच्छता एव आरोग्यस्य आधारः (cleanliness is the very basis of health).
ऋतुचर्या: The Indian year has six seasons (षड् ऋतवः): वसन्तः (spring), ग्रीष्मः (summer), वर्षा (rains), शरद् (autumn), हेमन्तः (early winter), शिशिरः (late winter). ऋतुचर्या (ऋतूनां चर्या) means adjusting food, dress and habits to the season: in ग्रीष्म, plenty of water, light food, protection from the sun; in वर्षा, boiled or clean water and freshly cooked food, since impure water spreads disease; in हेमन्त-शिशिर, warm clothing and nourishing food, for the digestive power is strong; in वसन्त, light food and exercise. The principle is simple: live with the season, not against it.

मनःस्वास्थ्यम् (Mental health)

Health is not of the body alone; शरीरस्य मनसः च स्वास्थ्यम् उभयम् आवश्यकम् — health of both body and mind is necessary, and each supports the other. Traditional means of keeping the mind healthy: सन्तोषः (contentment), ध्यानम् (meditation, sitting quietly with the breath), प्राणायामः (regulation of the breath), सत्सङ्गः (the company of good people), नियमितः क्रम (a regular routine), क्रोध-चिन्ता-वर्जनम् (avoiding anger and needless worry), and open conversation with family, teachers and friends when the mind is heavy.
The अमृतबिन्दु-उपनिषद् says: मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः — "the mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for human beings". A trained, calm mind is our best friend; an untrained mind our hardest burden.
The योगसूत्रम् (1.33) teaches चित्तप्रसादनम् — the calming/clarifying of the mind — through four attitudes: मैत्री (friendliness toward the happy), करुणा (compassion toward the suffering), मुदिता (gladness toward the virtuous), उपेक्षा (equanimity toward the wrongdoer). Practising these keeps the mind clear of envy, cruelty, jealousy and anger — the true toxins of मनःस्वास्थ्यम्.

व्याकरणम् (Grammar from the lesson)

(A) सन्धिः: मूलमुत्तमम् = मूलम् + उत्तमम्; शरीरमाद्यम् = शरीरम् + आद्यम्; रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः = रोगाः + तस्य + अपहर्तारः (विसर्ग-सन्धिः in रोगाः + तस्य → रोगास्तस्य; दीर्घ-सन्धिः in तस्य + अपहर्तारः → तस्यापहर्तारः, अ + अ = आ); युक्ताहारः = युक्त + आहारः (दीर्घ-सन्धिः, अ + आ = आ); सूर्योदयः = सूर्य + उदयः (गुण-सन्धिः, अ + उ = ओ); नास्ति = न + अस्ति (दीर्घ-सन्धिः). Splitting a joined form back into its parts is सन्धि-विच्छेदः.
(B) समासः: धर्मसाधनम् = धर्मस्य साधनम् (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः); दिनचर्या = दिनस्य चर्या (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः); ऋतुचर्या = ऋतूनां चर्या (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः); मिताहारः = मितः चासौ आहारः (कर्मधारयः); धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् = धर्मश्च अर्थश्च कामश्च मोक्षश्च, तेषाम् (द्वन्द्वः); युक्ताहारविहारस्य = युक्तौ आहारविहारौ यस्य सः, तस्य (बहुव्रीहिः — "of one whose food and recreation are regulated").
(C) विभक्तिः: आरोग्येण (तृतीया — "by health"); आरोग्याय (चतुर्थी — "for health"); रोगात् (पञ्चमी — "from disease"); मनसः / आरोग्यस्य (षष्ठी — "of the mind / of health"); शरीरे, प्रातःकाले, अजीर्णे (सप्तमी — "in the body, in the morning, when (food is) undigested" — note अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम् uses the locative to mean "in the condition of indigestion").
(D) कृदन्तः: क्त्वा-प्रत्ययः — स्नात्वा (having bathed), भुक्त्वा (having eaten), कृत्वा (having done); ल्यप्-प्रत्ययः — उत्थाय (having risen); तुमुन्-प्रत्ययः — रक्षितुम् (in order to protect: शरीरं रक्षितुं व्यायामः करणीयः), भोक्तुम् (in order to eat); क्त-प्रत्ययः — युक्तः (regulated), मितः (measured), जीर्णम् (digested).

सारांशः (Summary)

In this chapter you learned that आरोग्यम् — freedom from disease — is the highest happiness and the root of all four aims of life (Charaka), and that the body is the first instrument of dharma (Kalidasa). You read simple Sanskrit prose on दिनचर्या (early rising, cleanliness, exercise, timely food, timely sleep), the principles of आहार and मितभोजनम् (with the maxims अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम् and हितभुक् मितभुक् ऋतभुक्), the Gita's rule of regulated food, recreation, work, sleep and waking (6.17), the warning against all excess (अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत्), स्वच्छता and the six-season ऋतुचर्या, and the care of the mind — सन्तोष, ध्यान, प्राणायाम, सत्सङ्ग and the four attitudes of चित्तप्रसादनम्. From the same material you practised सन्धि and सन्धि-विच्छेद, समास identification, विभक्ति roles, and the कृदन्त forms क्त्वा, ल्यप्, तुमुन् and क्त. आरोग्यं परमं सुखम् — guard it daily, in body and in mind.

topics.name: आरोग्यस्य महत्त्वम् — The Importance of Health
topics.description: What आरोग्यम् (freedom from disease) means and why tradition calls it the highest happiness: आरोग्यं परमं भाग्यम्, Charaka's verse making health the root of the four पुरुषार्थs, and Kalidasa's शरीरमाद्यं खलु धर्मसाधनम्.

topics.name: दिनचर्या — The Daily Regimen
topics.description: The ordered conduct of the day: rising in ब्राह्ममुहूर्त, शौच and दन्तधावन, exercise, bath, prayer, study with a calm mind, timely moderate meals, evening play and timely sleep — read through simple Sanskrit prose with शब्दार्थ.

topics.name: आहारः मितभोजनं च — Diet and Moderate Eating
topics.description: Principles of wholesome diet: fresh simple food, seasonal fruits and vegetables, slow chewing, clean water, eating at regular times and in measured quantity; the maxims अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम् and हितभुक् मितभुक् ऋतभुक्; the verse अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत् on avoiding excess.

topics.name: निद्रा व्यायामः च — Sleep and Exercise
topics.description: The Gita's rule of the regulated life (युक्ताहारविहारस्य... योगो भवति दुःखहा, 6.17) with अन्वय and शब्दार्थ; the benefits of timely sufficient sleep and of regular gentle exercise — walking, योगासन, outdoor play — with moderation in both.

topics.name: स्वच्छता ऋतुचर्या च — Cleanliness and Seasonal Regimen
topics.description: Cleanliness as daily disease-prevention: washing hands before meals, clean clothes, clean surroundings, covered food and water; ऋतुचर्या — adjusting food, dress and habits to the six seasons (वसन्त, ग्रीष्म, वर्षा, शरद्, हेमन्त, शिशिर).

topics.name: मनःस्वास्थ्यम् — Mental Health
topics.description: Health of the mind and its bond with the body: सन्तोष, ध्यान, प्राणायाम, सत्सङ्ग, avoiding anger and worry; मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः; and the four attitudes of चित्तप्रसादनम् (मैत्री, करुणा, मुदिता, उपेक्षा) from योगसूत्र 1.33.

Recall the components and order of an ideal दिनचर्या — early rising, cleanliness, exercise, bath, prayer, study, timely meals, play and timely sleep — and the Sanskrit terms for each.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply the Gita's rule of regulated food, recreation, work, sleep and waking (6.17) to daily student life, and state the traditional benefits of timely sleep and regular moderate exercise.
