Analyse the relation between mind and body in health and the traditional means of mental well-being — सन्तोष, ध्यान, प्राणायाम, सत्सङ्ग and the four attitudes of चित्तप्रसादनम्.
Give the शब्दार्थ of words from the health verses, arrange a verse in अन्वय (prose order), and translate the verses of the chapter into simple English.
Perform सन्धि-विच्छेद, identify समास types (तत्पुरुष, कर्मधारय, द्वन्द्व, बहुव्रीहि), state विभक्ति roles, and recognise कृदन्त forms (क्त्वा, ल्यप्, तुमुन्, क्त) in words drawn from the chapter.

chapter_summary.title: आरोग्यं परमं सुखम् — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary covers Chapter 3: why health is the highest happiness, the traditional daily and seasonal regimens, wholesome diet, sleep, exercise, cleanliness and mental health — with the chapter's verses and the grammar drawn from them.

sections.heading: Health as the highest happiness
bullets: आरोग्यम् = the state of being free from disease (अरोग + ष्यञ्); tradition calls it the highest fortune — आरोग्यं परमं भाग्यं स्वास्थ्यं सर्वार्थसाधनम्.
Charaka (सूत्रस्थान 1.15): health is the best root of the four aims of life — धर्म, अर्थ, काम, मोक्ष; diseases are the robbers of health, welfare and life.
Kalidasa (कुमारसम्भव 5.33): शरीरमाद्यं खलु धर्मसाधनम् — the body is the first instrument of duty, so caring for it is itself part of धर्म.

sections.heading: दिनचर्या — the ordered day
bullets: Rise in ब्राह्ममुहूर्त (before sunrise); perform शौच and दन्तधावन; do light व्यायाम or योगासन; bathe (स्नात्वा) and pray.
Study with a calm mind (शान्तमनसा अध्ययनम्); eat moderate wholesome food at fixed times (समये मितं हितं च भोजनम्).
Play in the evening (सायं क्रीडति) and sleep at a fixed time (रात्रौ समये शयनम्) — regularity keeps body and mind in rhythm.
दिनचर्या = दिनस्य चर्या, a षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष compound meaning 'the conduct of the day'.

sections.heading: आहार, moderation and the warning against excess
bullets: Eat fresh simple food, seasonal fruits and vegetables, chew slowly, drink clean water, and practise मितभोजनम् — stop a little before fullness.
अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम् — eating again while the earlier meal is undigested is poison; the ideal eater is हितभुक् मितभुक् ऋतभुक्.
Charaka's three pillars of health (त्रयः उपस्तम्भाः): आहार (food), स्वप्न (sleep), ब्रह्मचर्य (disciplined living).
अतिदानाद् बलिर्बद्धो... अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत् — Bali, Suyodhana and Ravana were ruined by excess; avoid excess in everything, including food.

sections.heading: Sleep, exercise and the Gita's rule of balance
bullets: Gita 6.17: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा — for one regulated in food, recreation, work, sleep and waking, yoga destroys sorrow.
Timely, sufficient निद्रा repairs the body and refreshes memory and attention; late and irregular sleep dulls both.
व्यायामेन शरीरं दृढं भवति — exercise firms the body, kindles digestion and cheers the mind; walking, योगासन and outdoor games in moderation are ideal.

sections.heading: Cleanliness, the seasons and the mind
bullets: स्वच्छता is daily disease-prevention: wash hands before meals (भोजनात् पूर्वं हस्तौ प्रक्षालयेत्), wear clean clothes, keep surroundings clean, cover food and water.
ऋतुचर्या: adapt to the six seasons — much water and light food in ग्रीष्म, boiled water in वर्षा, nourishing food and warm clothing in हेमन्त-शिशिर.
मनःस्वास्थ्यम्: सन्तोष, ध्यान, प्राणायाम, सत्सङ्ग, a regular routine and avoiding anger and worry keep the mind healthy; mind and body support each other.
मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः; योगसूत्र 1.33 gives four attitudes for चित्तप्रसादनम् — मैत्री, करुणा, मुदिता, उपेक्षा.

key_takeaways: आरोग्यम् (freedom from disease) is the highest happiness and the best root of all four aims of life — धर्म, अर्थ, काम, मोक्ष.
The body is the first instrument of duty (शरीरमाद्यं खलु धर्मसाधनम्), so its care is itself धर्म.
A regular दिनचर्या — early rising, cleanliness, exercise, timely food and timely sleep — keeps body and mind in rhythm.
Eat मितं हितं च — measured and wholesome; अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम् warns against eating over undigested food, and अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत् against all excess.
Gita 6.17: balance in food, recreation, work, sleep and waking makes discipline the destroyer of sorrow (दुःखहा).
स्वच्छता and season-wise living (ऋतुचर्या over the six ऋतुs) prevent disease before it starts.
The mind is the cause of bondage and freedom (मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः); सन्तोष, ध्यान, प्राणायाम, सत्सङ्ग and the four attitudes of चित्तप्रसादनम् keep it healthy.

glossary.definition: Health; the state of being free from disease (रोगाभावः), formed from अरोग with the abstract suffix ष्यञ्.
The daily regimen — the ordered conduct (चर्या) of the day (दिनस्य); a षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष compound.
The seasonal regimen — adjusting food, dress and habits to each of the six seasons (षड् ऋतवः).
Moderate eating — taking food in measured quantity, stopping a little before the stomach is full.
Traditional maxim: 'when the earlier food is undigested, eating (again) is poison' — a warning against untimely overeating.
Description of the disciplined eater: one who eats what is wholesome, eats moderately, and eats what is honestly earned.
The auspicious period before sunrise, recommended for rising, prayer and study.
Physical exercise — walking, yoga postures, games — which firms the body, aids digestion and cheers the mind.
Sleep; one of Charaka's three pillars of health, to be taken and left at regular times.
Cleanliness — of hands, clothes, food, water and surroundings; daily prevention of disease.
Mental health — the calm, contented state of mind maintained by सन्तोष, ध्यान, प्राणायाम and सत्सङ्ग.
'Destroyer of sorrow' — the Gita's word (6.17) for yoga practised by one regulated in food, recreation, work, sleep and waking.
An aim of human life; the four are धर्म (duty), अर्थ (wealth), काम (desire) and मोक्ष (liberation).
The calming and clarifying of the mind (योगसूत्र 1.33) through मैत्री, करुणा, मुदिता and उपेक्षा.
A word formed from a verbal root with a krt suffix, e.g. स्नात्वा (क्त्वा), उत्थाय (ल्यप्), रक्षितुम् (तुमुन्), युक्तः (क्त).

worksheet.title: Worksheet — आरोग्यं परमं सुखम् (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 3)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give explanations in English. Refer to the verses and the prose passage of the lesson where needed.

questions.question:
Translate into simple English and give the अन्वय:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् आरोग्यं मूलमुत्तमम् ।
रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः श्रेयसो जीवितस्य च ॥
questions.answer:
अन्वय: आरोग्यं धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् उत्तमं मूलम् (अस्ति)। रोगाः तस्य श्रेयसः जीवितस्य च अपहर्तारः (भवन्ति)।
Translation: Health is the best root of the four aims of life — duty (धर्म), wealth (अर्थ), desire (काम) and liberation (मोक्ष). Diseases are the robbers of that health, of welfare, and of life itself.
questions.explanation: Charaka Samhita, Sutrasthana 1.15 — health as the foundation of all four पुरुषार्थs.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of each: आरोग्यम्, मूलम्, अपहर्तारः, दुःखहा, वर्जयेत्.
questions.answer: आरोग्यम् = health, freedom from disease; मूलम् = root, foundation; अपहर्तारः = takers-away, robbers; दुःखहा = destroyer of sorrow; वर्जयेत् = one should avoid.
questions.explanation: Key vocabulary from the three main verses of the chapter.

questions.question: The maxim 'अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम्' teaches that
options: eating while the previous meal is undigested is like poison
poisonous food must never be eaten
one should eat only once a day
food loses its taste when kept overnight
questions.answer: eating while the previous meal is undigested is like poison
questions.explanation: अजीर्णे (locative: 'when undigested') भोजनम् (eating) विषम् (is poison) — a warning against untimely overeating.

questions.question: Complete the pada of Kalidasa: शरीरमाद्यं खलु ________ ।
questions.explanation: कुमारसम्भवम् 5.33 — the body is indeed the first instrument of dharma.

questions.question: According to Bhagavad Gita 6.17, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow for one whose food, recreation, effort in work, sleep and waking are all regulated (युक्त).
questions.explanation: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा — balance in all five makes yoga दुःखहा.

questions.question: Describe, in four or five points, the दिनचर्या of the ideal student given in the lesson's prose passage. Use at least four Sanskrit terms from the passage.
questions.answer: (1) He rises from bed in the ब्राह्ममुहूर्त, before sunrise (प्रातः उत्तिष्ठति). (2) He performs शौच and दन्तधावन, then light व्यायाम or योगासन. (3) स्नात्वा (having bathed) he prays and studies with a calm mind (शान्तमनसा अध्ययनम्). (4) He eats मितं हितं च भोजनम् at the proper time (समये). (5) In the evening he plays (क्रीडाङ्गणे क्रीडति) and at night sleeps at a fixed time (समये शयनम्).
questions.explanation: The five-part rhythm of the ideal day: rising, cleanliness and exercise, study, timely food, play and timely sleep.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) मूलमुत्तमम् (b) सूर्योदयः, and name the सन्धि in (b).
questions.answer: (a) मूलमुत्तमम् = मूलम् + उत्तमम्. (b) सूर्योदयः = सूर्य + उदयः — गुण-सन्धिः (अ + उ = ओ).
questions.explanation: In (a) the final म् joins the following vowel; in (b) अ + उ combine to ओ by guna sandhi.

questions.question: 'आरोग्यं परमं सुखम्' — justify this statement in an essay of 10-12 sentences, citing and explaining at least two verses from the chapter (e.g. Charaka's धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम्... and Kalidasa's शरीरमाद्यं खलु धर्मसाधनम्).
questions.answer: Health is rightly called the highest happiness because every other good of life depends on it. The traditional maxim says आरोग्यं परमं भाग्यं स्वास्थ्यं सर्वार्थसाधनम् — health is the highest fortune and the instrument of all achievement. Charaka goes further: आरोग्यं धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् उत्तमं मूलम् — health is the best root of the four aims of life; without it one can neither perform duty, nor earn wealth, nor enjoy legitimate pleasures, nor pursue liberation. He adds that diseases are अपहर्तारः — robbers — of health, welfare and life itself. Kalidasa's line शरीरमाद्यं खलु धर्मसाधनम् teaches that the body is the first instrument of dharma: even the noblest work needs a healthy body as its tool, so caring for the body is itself a duty, not a luxury. A wealthy but sick person cannot enjoy wealth; a learned but exhausted person cannot use learning. Health, once lost, makes every possession tasteless, while a healthy person with simple means can study, serve, work and remain cheerful. Therefore the daily disciplines of the chapter — दिनचर्या, मित-आहार, निद्रा, व्यायाम, स्वच्छता and care of the mind — are not small habits but the very foundation of a good life. In this sense आरोग्यम् is truly परमं सुखम् — the happiness on which all other happiness stands.
questions.explanation: The essay should define आरोग्य, cite two verses with meaning, and argue that all other goods depend on health.

questions.question: What is मनःस्वास्थ्यम्? Explain four traditional means of keeping the mind healthy, and the four attitudes of चित्तप्रसादनम् taught in योगसूत्र 1.33.
questions.answer: मनःस्वास्थ्यम् is the health of the mind — a calm, contented, steady inner state — and it supports bodily health just as bodily health supports it. Four traditional means: (1) सन्तोषः — contentment, not endlessly comparing oneself with others; (2) ध्यानम् — sitting quietly in meditation, watching the breath; (3) प्राणायामः — gentle regulation of the breath, which settles the mind; (4) सत्सङ्गः — the company of good people, along with a regular routine and openly sharing worries with family and teachers, while avoiding क्रोध (anger) and needless चिन्ता (worry). योगसूत्र 1.33 teaches चित्तप्रसादनम् — clarity and calm of mind — through four attitudes: मैत्री, friendliness toward the happy; करुणा, compassion toward the suffering; मुदिता, gladness at the virtuous; and उपेक्षा, equanimity toward the wrongdoer. Practising these removes envy, cruelty, jealousy and resentment — the real toxins of the mind — as the Upanishad says, मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः.
questions.explanation: Define मनःस्वास्थ्य, give four means (सन्तोष, ध्यान, प्राणायाम, सत्सङ्ग), and explain मैत्री-करुणा-मुदिता-उपेक्षा.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions:
'रमेशः रात्रौ बहुकालं चलदूरवाणीं पश्यति, विलम्बेन शेते, प्रातः विलम्बेन उत्तिष्ठति च। सः व्यायामं न करोति, समये भोजनं न भुङ्क्ते, बहु च खादति। सः सर्वदा श्रान्तः भवति, पठने च मनः न लगति।'
(a) Which rules of दिनचर्या is Ramesh breaking? (b) Which line of Gita 6.17 does his lifestyle violate? (c) Suggest three changes, using Sanskrit terms from the lesson.
questions.answer: (a) He breaks the rules of timely sleep and timely rising (समये शयनम्, ब्राह्ममुहूर्ते उत्थानम्), of daily व्यायाम, and of timely, moderate food (समये मितं भोजनम्) — instead he overeats and stays up watching his phone. (b) His life violates युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य (regulated sleep and waking) and युक्ताहारविहारस्य (regulated food and recreation) — Gita 6.17 says yoga is दुःखहा only for one who is युक्त in these. (c) Three changes: sleep and rise at fixed times (समये शयनम् उत्थानं च); do daily moderate exercise (प्रतिदिनं व्यायामः / योगासनम्); eat measured wholesome food at fixed times (समये मितं हितं च भोजनम्) and limit late-night screen time (recreation, विहार, in moderation). His tiredness and poor concentration are the natural fruit of an unregulated routine.
questions.explanation: The case applies दिनचर्या and Gita 6.17 to a familiar student lifestyle problem.

questions.question: The word आरोग्यम् means
questions.explanation: आरोग्यम् = रोगाभावः, the state of being free from disease (अरोग + ष्यञ्).

questions.question: Complete the maxim: आरोग्यं परमं भाग्यं ________ ।
questions.explanation: Health is the highest fortune; well-being is the means of achieving all aims.

questions.question: According to the Charaka verse in the lesson, आरोग्यम् is the उत्तमं मूलम् (best root) of
questions.explanation: धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् आरोग्यं मूलमुत्तमम् — health is the root of all four पुरुषार्थs.

questions.question: In the Charaka verse, diseases (रोगाः) are called
options: अपहर्तारः — robbers (of health, welfare and life)
questions.answer: अपहर्तारः — robbers (of health, welfare and life)
questions.explanation: रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः श्रेयसो जीवितस्य च — diseases rob health, welfare and life.

questions.question: The line 'शरीरमाद्यं खलु धर्मसाधनम्' comes from
questions.explanation: It is a famous pada from Kumarasambhava 5.33.

questions.question: 'शरीरमाद्यं खलु धर्मसाधनम्' means
options: the body is indeed the first instrument of duty
the body is the greatest obstacle to duty
duty is more important than the body
the body should be decorated first
questions.answer: the body is indeed the first instrument of duty
questions.explanation: शरीरम् (body) आद्यम् (first) खलु (indeed) धर्मसाधनम् (instrument of dharma) — even noble work needs a healthy body.

questions.question: Grammatically, आरोग्यम् is derived as
options: अरोग + ष्यञ् (taddhita) — 'the state of one free from disease'
questions.answer: अरोग + ष्यञ् (taddhita) — 'the state of one free from disease'
questions.explanation: अरोगः (free of disease) + abstract suffix ष्यञ् gives आरोग्यम् = रोगाभावः.

questions.question: Why is स्वास्थ्यम् called सर्वार्थसाधनम् in the lesson?
options: because every goal of life — study, work, duty, joy — needs health as its instrument
because health can be bought with wealth
because healthy people need no goals
because only saints can be healthy
questions.answer: because every goal of life — study, work, duty, joy — needs health as its instrument
questions.explanation: सर्व (all) + अर्थ (aims) + साधनम् (means): without health no aim can be accomplished.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the four पुरुषार्थs named in the Charaka verse?
questions.explanation: The four पुरुषार्थs are धर्म, अर्थ, काम and मोक्ष; fame is not among them.

questions.question: दिनचर्या means
questions.explanation: दिनस्य चर्या = the ordered conduct of the day's activities.

questions.question: ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते refers to
questions.explanation: ब्राह्ममुहूर्त is the early period before sunrise, ideal for rising, prayer and study.

questions.question: दन्तधावनम् means
questions.explanation: दन्त (teeth) + धावन (cleaning/washing) — part of the morning routine.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly follows the prose passage's morning order?
options: उत्थानम् → शौच-दन्तधावनम् → व्यायामः → स्नानम् → प्रार्थना → अध्ययनम्
अध्ययनम् → स्नानम् → उत्थानम् → व्यायामः → प्रार्थना → शौचम्
स्नानम् → उत्थानम् → भोजनम् → शयनम् → व्यायामः → प्रार्थना
प्रार्थना → शयनम् → उत्थानम् → क्रीडा → स्नानम् → भोजनम्
questions.answer: उत्थानम् → शौच-दन्तधावनम् → व्यायामः → स्नानम् → प्रार्थना → अध्ययनम्
questions.explanation: The passage: rises, performs ablutions and tooth-cleaning, exercises, bathes (स्नात्वा), prays, then studies.

questions.question: The compound दिनचर्या is analysed as दिनस्य चर्या. It is therefore a
questions.explanation: The first member stands in the genitive relation (दिनस्य) to the second — hence षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष.

questions.question: In 'सः शय्यायाः उत्तिष्ठति', the verb उत्तिष्ठति means
questions.explanation: उद् + स्था → उत्तिष्ठति, 'he gets up (from the bed, शय्यायाः)'.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of the दिनचर्या described in the lesson?
options: रात्रौ बहुकालं जागरणम् (staying awake late into the night)
समये भोजनम् (eating at the proper time)
questions.answer: रात्रौ बहुकालं जागरणम् (staying awake late into the night)
questions.explanation: The lesson prescribes timely sleep (समये शयनम्), not late waking.

questions.question: स्नात्वा means
questions.explanation: स्ना (to bathe) + क्त्वा = स्नात्वा, 'having bathed'.

questions.question: According to the lesson, why is early rising beneficial for a student?
options: it gives fresh air, quiet time for study and an unhurried start to the day
it makes afternoon naps unnecessary forever
it is required only during examinations
questions.answer: it gives fresh air, quiet time for study and an unhurried start to the day
questions.explanation: The ब्राह्ममुहूर्त offers calm, freshness and time — ideal conditions for prayer and study.

questions.question: In the prose passage, what does the ideal student do in the evening (सायम्)?
options: क्रीडाङ्गणे क्रीडति — he plays on the playground
विद्यालयं गच्छति — he goes to school
ग्रन्थं रचयति — he composes a book
questions.answer: क्रीडाङ्गणे क्रीडति — he plays on the playground
questions.explanation: सायं सः क्रीडाङ्गणे क्रीडति — evening play balances the day's study.

questions.question: मितभोजनम् means
questions.explanation: मित (measured) + भोजन (eating) — stopping a little before the stomach is full.

questions.question: अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम् — here अजीर्णे means
options: when the (earlier) food is still undigested
questions.answer: when the (earlier) food is still undigested
questions.explanation: अजीर्ण = undigested; the locative अजीर्णे means 'in the state of indigestion'.

questions.question: In the phrase हितभुक् मितभुक् ऋतभुक्, the word ऋतभुक् means one who
questions.explanation: ऋत = right/truthful; ऋतभुक् = one whose food is righteously, honestly obtained.

questions.question: The teaching 'अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत्' means
options: one should avoid excess in everything
questions.answer: one should avoid excess in everything
questions.explanation: अति (excess) सर्वत्र (everywhere) वर्जयेत् (one should avoid) — moderation is the rule.

questions.question: According to the moderation verse, King Bali was bound (बद्धः) because of
questions.explanation: अतिदानाद् बलिर्बद्धः — even generosity in excess brought Bali's bondage.

questions.question: In the same verse, रावणः was slain because of
questions.explanation: अतिलौल्याद् रावणो हतः — Ravana perished through excessive greed.

questions.question: Which of these best matches the lesson's principles of good आहार?
options: fresh simple food, seasonal fruits and vegetables, slow chewing, clean water
questions.answer: fresh simple food, seasonal fruits and vegetables, slow chewing, clean water
questions.explanation: The lesson lists freshness, seasonality, slow chewing, clean water, moderation and regular timing.

questions.question: The Charaka tradition names three pillars (त्रयः उपस्तम्भाः) of health. They are
questions.explanation: Food, sleep and disciplined living are the three supports that hold up the house of health.

questions.question: मिताहारः is analysed as मितः चासौ आहारः. The compound is a
questions.explanation: Adjective + noun in apposition (measured food) — a कर्मधारय (descriptive) compound.

questions.question: In अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम्, the word अजीर्णे stands in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: The locative expresses the condition: 'in (the state of) indigestion'.

questions.question: According to Gita 6.17, for the person who is युक्त in food, recreation, work, sleep and waking, योगः becomes
questions.explanation: युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा — discipline with balance ends sorrow.

questions.question: In युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य, the pair स्वप्न and अवबोध mean
questions.explanation: स्वप्न = sleep; अवबोध = waking — both must be regulated (युक्त).

questions.question: The word दुःखहा literally means
questions.explanation: हा (from हन्, to strike/destroy) at the end of a compound = 'destroyer of'.

questions.question: According to the lesson, व्यायामेन (by exercise)
options: the body becomes firm, digestion strengthens and the mind becomes cheerful
the body becomes weak and the mind dull
questions.answer: the body becomes firm, digestion strengthens and the mind becomes cheerful
questions.explanation: व्यायामेन शरीरं दृढं भवति, जाठराग्निः वर्धते, मनः च प्रसन्नं भवति।

questions.question: Why is timely, sufficient निद्रा (sleep) important according to the lesson?
options: it repairs the body and refreshes memory and attention
it replaces the need for food
it is useful only for small children
questions.answer: it repairs the body and refreshes memory and attention
questions.explanation: Late and irregular sleep dulls memory and attention; timely sleep restores them.

questions.question: The verse युक्ताहारविहारस्य... occurs in which chapter of the Bhagavad Gita?
questions.explanation: It is Bhagavad Gita 6.17, in the chapter on ध्यानयोग.

questions.question: In Gita 6.17 the repeated word युक्त means
questions.explanation: युक्त (from युज्) = properly joined/regulated — neither too much nor too little.

questions.question: Which habit best follows the lesson's guidance on sleep?
options: समये शयनं समये उत्थानं च — sleeping and rising at fixed times
sleeping very late and rising at noon
studying all night before every examination
questions.answer: समये शयनं समये उत्थानं च — sleeping and rising at fixed times
questions.explanation: Regular timing of sleep and rising protects health (आरोग्यस्य रक्षकम्).

questions.question: In युक्ताहारविहारस्य, विहार means
questions.explanation: Here विहार = recreation/moving about for refreshment, paired with आहार (food).

questions.question: ऋतुचर्या means
options: the seasonal regimen — adjusting habits to each season
questions.answer: the seasonal regimen — adjusting habits to each season
questions.explanation: ऋतूनां चर्या — the conduct suited to the seasons.

questions.question: How many seasons (ऋतवः) does the Indian year have according to the lesson?
questions.explanation: षड् ऋतवः: वसन्त, ग्रीष्म, वर्षा, शरद्, हेमन्त, शिशिर.

questions.question: स्वच्छता means
questions.explanation: स्वच्छ (clean) + ता (abstract suffix) = cleanliness.

questions.question: भोजनात् पूर्वं हस्तौ प्रक्षालयेत् — this instruction tells us to
options: dry the hands in the sun
questions.explanation: भोजनात् पूर्वम् = before food; हस्तौ प्रक्षालयेत् = one should wash the two hands.

questions.question: According to the lesson's ऋतुचर्या, in ग्रीष्म (summer) one should take
options: plenty of water, light food and protection from the sun
heavy fried food and thick woollens
questions.answer: plenty of water, light food and protection from the sun
questions.explanation: Summer regimen: hydration, light diet, shade — live with the season.

questions.question: In हेमन्त-शिशिर (winter), the lesson recommends
options: warm clothing and nourishing food, since digestion is strong
questions.answer: warm clothing and nourishing food, since digestion is strong
questions.explanation: Winter's strong digestive power suits nourishing food; warm clothing protects the body.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the six ऋतुs?
questions.explanation: मकर is a zodiac sign (Capricorn), not a season; the six ऋतुs are वसन्त, ग्रीष्म, वर्षा, शरद्, हेमन्त, शिशिर.

questions.question: Why does the lesson call स्वच्छता 'disease-prevention in daily action'?
options: because much disease travels through unclean hands, water and surroundings
because clean clothes are more fashionable
because cleanliness replaces the need for exercise
questions.answer: because much disease travels through unclean hands, water and surroundings
questions.explanation: Washing hands, clean water and clean surroundings stop disease before it starts.

questions.question: In वर्षा (the rainy season), the lesson especially advises
options: boiled or clean water and freshly cooked food
eating stale food to save time
questions.answer: boiled or clean water and freshly cooked food
questions.explanation: Impure water spreads disease most in the rains, so water discipline matters most then.

questions.question: मनःस्वास्थ्यम् means
questions.explanation: मनस् (mind) + स्वास्थ्य (health/well-being) = mental health.

questions.question: 'मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः' means
options: the mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for human beings
human beings can never control the mind
bondage and liberation do not exist
questions.answer: the mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for human beings
questions.explanation: मन एव (the mind alone) कारणम् (the cause) बन्धमोक्षयोः (of bondage and liberation) — from the अमृतबिन्दु-उपनिषद्.

questions.question: ध्यानम् means
questions.explanation: ध्यानम् = sitting quietly in meditation, e.g. watching the breath.

questions.question: सन्तोषः means
questions.explanation: सन्तोष = contentment — not endlessly comparing oneself with others.

questions.question: Which of the following harms मनःस्वास्थ्यम् according to the lesson?
options: क्रोधः and needless चिन्ता (anger and worry)
questions.answer: क्रोधः and needless चिन्ता (anger and worry)
questions.explanation: The lesson prescribes क्रोध-चिन्ता-वर्जनम् — avoiding anger and needless worry.

questions.question: प्राणायामः is
questions.explanation: प्राण (breath/life-force) + आयाम (extension/regulation) — gentle breath discipline that settles the mind.

questions.question: योगसूत्र 1.33 teaches चित्तप्रसादनम् through four attitudes. They are
questions.explanation: Friendliness toward the happy, compassion for the suffering, gladness at the virtuous, equanimity toward the wrongdoer.

questions.question: सत्सङ्गः means
questions.explanation: सत् (good) + सङ्ग (association) — good company nourishes the mind.

questions.question: What does the lesson say about the relation between mind and body in health?
options: health of both is necessary, and each supports the other
questions.answer: health of both is necessary, and each supports the other
questions.explanation: शरीरस्य मनसः च स्वास्थ्यम् उभयम् आवश्यकम् — the two healths sustain each other.

questions.question: The शब्दार्थ of अपहर्तारः is
questions.explanation: अप + हृ (to take away) + तृच् — 'those who carry off'; diseases rob health, welfare and life.

questions.question: मूलम् means
questions.explanation: In the Charaka verse, health is the मूलम् — the root — of the four aims of life.

questions.question: In रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः श्रेयसो जीवितस्य च, the word श्रेयसः means
questions.explanation: श्रेयस् = the good, welfare; here genitive singular — diseases rob (one) of welfare too.

questions.question: Which is the correct अन्वय of धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् आरोग्यं मूलमुत्तमम्?
questions.explanation: Subject आरोग्यम्; predicate उत्तमं मूलम्; genitive धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् qualifies मूलम्.

questions.question: सर्वार्थसाधनम् is best translated as
options: the means of accomplishing all aims
questions.answer: the means of accomplishing all aims
questions.explanation: सर्व (all) + अर्थ (aims) + साधनम् (instrument/means).

questions.question: The form युक्ताहारविहारस्य in Gita 6.17 is in the षष्ठी (genitive) because it means
options: 'of one whose food and recreation are regulated' — yoga becomes दुःखहा for such a person
questions.answer: 'of one whose food and recreation are regulated' — yoga becomes दुःखहा for such a person
questions.explanation: The genitive qualifies the implied person (पुरुषस्य): his yoga destroys sorrow.

questions.question: In शरीरमाद्यं खलु धर्मसाधनम्, the word खलु means
questions.explanation: खलु is an emphatic particle: 'the body is INDEED the first instrument of dharma'.

questions.question: आद्यम् means
questions.explanation: आद्य (from आदि, beginning) = first; the body is the FIRST instrument of duty.

questions.question: The verb form वर्जयेत् (in अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत्) is
questions.explanation: The optative (विधिलिङ्) expresses an injunction: one SHOULD avoid excess.

questions.question: भाग्यम् (in आरोग्यं परमं भाग्यम्) means
questions.explanation: Health is called the highest भाग्य — the supreme good fortune.

questions.question: The correct सन्धि-विच्छेद of मूलमुत्तमम् is
questions.explanation: The final म् of मूलम् joins the initial उ of उत्तमम्.

questions.question: सूर्योदयः = सूर्य + उदयः is an example of
questions.explanation: अ + उ combine into the guna vowel ओ: sūrya + udayaḥ → sūryodayaḥ.

questions.question: The सन्धि-विच्छेद of शरीरमाद्यम् is
questions.explanation: शरीरम् (the body) + आद्यम् (first) join in the verse pada.

questions.question: धर्मसाधनम्, analysed as धर्मस्य साधनम्, is which समास?
questions.explanation: The first member bears a genitive relation (धर्मस्य) to the second — a षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष.

questions.question: धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् (धर्मश्च अर्थश्च कामश्च मोक्षश्च, तेषाम्) is which समास?
questions.explanation: Four coordinate members joined by 'and' — an itaretara द्वन्द्व compound.

questions.question: The suffix in स्नात्वा ('having bathed') is
questions.explanation: स्ना + क्त्वा = स्नात्वा — the absolutive 'having bathed'.

questions.question: रक्षितुम् (as in शरीरं रक्षितुं व्यायामः करणीयः) means
questions.explanation: रक्ष् + तुमुन् = रक्षितुम्, the infinitive of purpose: 'to protect (the body)'.

questions.question: आरोग्येण ('by health') is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: The instrumental -एण ending expresses the means: 'by/through health'.

questions.question: भुक्त्वा means
questions.explanation: भुज् + क्त्वा = भुक्त्वा — 'having eaten'.

questions.question: आरोग्यम् means the state of being free from disease (रोगाभावः).
questions.explanation: आरोग्यम् is derived from अरोग (free of disease) with the abstract suffix ष्यञ्.

questions.question: According to the Charaka verse, diseases (रोगाः) are the takers-away (अपहर्तारः) of health, welfare and life.
questions.explanation: रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः श्रेयसो जीवितस्य च — diseases rob health, welfare and life.

questions.question: Gita 6.17 teaches that yoga destroys sorrow only for one who fasts completely and gives up sleep.
questions.explanation: The verse prescribes REGULATED (युक्त) food, recreation, work, sleep and waking — balance, not total denial.

questions.question: The maxim अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम् encourages us to eat again quickly even when the earlier meal is undigested.
questions.explanation: It warns the opposite: eating over undigested food is like poison.

questions.question: दिनचर्या means the seasonal regimen followed over the six seasons.
questions.explanation: दिनचर्या is the DAILY regimen (दिनस्य चर्या); the seasonal regimen is ऋतुचर्या.

questions.question: According to the lesson, the Indian year has six seasons (षड् ऋतवः).
questions.explanation: वसन्त, ग्रीष्म, वर्षा, शरद्, हेमन्त and शिशिर are the six ऋतुs.

questions.question: The pada शरीरमाद्यं खलु धर्मसाधनम् is from Kalidasa's Kumarasambhava.
questions.explanation: It occurs at Kumarasambhava 5.33, in the description of Parvati's austerities.

questions.question: According to the lesson, cultivating क्रोध (anger) and चिन्ता (worry) improves mental health.
questions.explanation: The lesson prescribes क्रोध-चिन्ता-वर्जनम् — anger and needless worry are to be avoided.

questions.question: सूर्योदयः is formed from सूर्य + उदयः by गुण-सन्धि (अ + उ = ओ).
questions.explanation: अ + उ yields the guna vowel ओ — a standard गुण-सन्धि.

questions.question: In the moderation verse, Bali was bound because of excessive pride (अतिमानात्).
questions.explanation: Bali was bound through excessive GIVING (अतिदानात्); it was Suyodhana who fell through excessive pride.

questions.question: Complete the maxim: आरोग्यं परमं ________ स्वास्थ्यं सर्वार्थसाधनम् ।
questions.explanation: आरोग्यं परमं भाग्यम् — health is the highest fortune.

questions.question: Complete the Charaka verse: धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् आरोग्यं ________ उत्तमम् ।
questions.explanation: Health is the best ROOT (मूलम्) of the four aims of life.

questions.question: Complete Kalidasa's pada: शरीरमाद्यं खलु ________ ।
questions.explanation: The body is indeed the first instrument of dharma (धर्मसाधनम्).

questions.question: Complete the maxim: अजीर्णे भोजनं ________ ।
questions.explanation: Eating over undigested food is poison (विषम्).

questions.question: Complete the teaching of the moderation verse: अति सर्वत्र ________ ।
questions.explanation: One should AVOID (वर्जयेत्) excess in everything.

questions.question: Complete Gita 6.17: युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति ________ ।
questions.explanation: For the regulated person, yoga becomes दुःखहा — the destroyer of sorrow.

questions.question: दिनस्य चर्या इति ________ । (Give the compound word meaning 'the daily regimen'.)
questions.explanation: दिनस्य चर्या contracts into the षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष compound दिनचर्या.

questions.question: Complete from the prose passage: आदर्शः छात्रः प्रातः ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते शय्यायाः ________ ।
questions.explanation: The ideal student RISES (उत्तिष्ठति) from bed in the brahma-muhurta.

questions.question: Complete the rule of cleanliness: भोजनात् पूर्वं हस्तौ ________ ।
questions.explanation: Before food one SHOULD WASH (प्रक्षालयेत्) the hands.

questions.question: ऋतूनां संख्या ________ अस्ति। (How many seasons? Answer with the Sanskrit numeral.)
questions.explanation: There are SIX (षट्) seasons — षड् ऋतवः.

questions.question: Complete the Upanishadic line: मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं ________ ।
questions.explanation: The mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation (बन्धमोक्षयोः).

questions.question: स्नात्वा ('having bathed') इत्यत्र ________ प्रत्ययः अस्ति। (Name the suffix.)
questions.explanation: स्ना + क्त्वा = स्नात्वा — the absolutive suffix क्त्वा.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदं पूरयत: मूलमुत्तमम् = मूलम् + ________ ।
questions.explanation: मूलम् + उत्तमम् join in the verse as मूलमुत्तमम्.

questions.question: धर्मसाधनम् (धर्मस्य साधनम्) इत्यत्र ________ समासः अस्ति। (Name the broad compound type.)
questions.explanation: A genitive relation between the members makes it a (षष्ठी-)तत्पुरुष compound.

questions.question: Complete the Charaka verse: रोगास्तस्य ________ श्रेयसो जीवितस्य च ।
questions.explanation: Diseases are the ROBBERS (अपहर्तारः) of health, welfare and life.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of the chapter's title, आरोग्यं परमं सुखम्, in two or three sentences.
questions.answer: The title means 'health is the highest happiness'. आरोग्यम् is the state of being free from disease; it is called परमं सुखम् because every other joy — study, work, play, wealth — can be enjoyed only by a healthy person. A sick person possesses things but cannot enjoy them, so health is the happiness on which all other happiness rests.
questions.explanation: Definition of आरोग्य plus the reason it is ranked above all other pleasures.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of Charaka's verse धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् आरोग्यं मूलमुत्तमम्... in your own words. Why does he call diseases अपहर्तारः?
questions.answer: Charaka says health is the best root (उत्तमं मूलम्) of the four aims of human life — धर्म (duty), अर्थ (wealth), काम (legitimate desire) and मोक्ष (liberation): none of the four can be pursued without a healthy body and mind. He calls diseases अपहर्तारः, 'robbers', because they steal three things at once — health itself, our welfare (श्रेयस्), and even life (जीवितम्). Disease is thus not a small inconvenience but a thief of everything valuable.
questions.explanation: Health as foundation of the four पुरुषार्थs; diseases as robbers of health, welfare and life.

questions.question: Kalidasa says शरीरमाद्यं खलु धर्मसाधनम्. How does this line answer someone who thinks caring for the body is mere vanity?
questions.answer: The line says the body is the FIRST instrument (आद्यं साधनम्) of धर्म: every duty — study, service, work, worship — must be performed through the body. Therefore keeping the body healthy is not vanity or self-indulgence; it is the necessary maintenance of the very tool of righteous action. Neglecting health actually harms one's ability to do one's duty.
questions.explanation: Body as the instrument of dharma — its care is duty, not decoration.

questions.question: Translate the following prose lines into English: 'आदर्शः छात्रः प्रातः ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते शय्यायाः उत्तिष्ठति। स्नात्वा सः प्रार्थनां करोति। सः समये मितं हितं च भोजनं भुङ्क्ते।'
questions.answer: The ideal student rises from bed early in the morning, in the brahma-muhurta (before sunrise). Having bathed, he performs his prayer. He eats measured (moderate) and wholesome food at the proper time.
questions.explanation: उत्तिष्ठति = rises; स्नात्वा = having bathed; मितं हितं च भोजनम् = moderate and wholesome food; समये = at the right time.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: शय्यायाः, दन्तधावनम्, शान्तमनसा, क्रीडाङ्गणे.
questions.answer: शय्यायाः = from the bed; दन्तधावनम् = cleaning of the teeth; शान्तमनसा = with a calm mind; क्रीडाङ्गणे = on the playground.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from the दिनचर्या prose passage.

questions.question: Why does the lesson recommend rising in the ब्राह्ममुहूर्त? Give three benefits.
questions.answer: (1) The pre-dawn air is fresh and the surroundings are quiet, which is ideal for prayer, प्राणायाम and study. (2) The mind is calm and memory is sharp at that hour, so what is studied is well retained. (3) Rising early gives an unhurried start — time for शौच, दन्तधावन, व्यायाम and bath before the day's work — keeping the whole दिनचर्या in rhythm.
questions.explanation: Freshness, mental clarity and an unhurried, regular start are the traditional benefits.

questions.question: What is मितभोजनम्? Give any three principles of good आहार from the lesson.
questions.answer: मितभोजनम् is eating in measured quantity — stopping a little before the stomach is completely full. Three principles of good आहार: (1) eat fresh, simple food and seasonal fruits and vegetables; (2) chew slowly and well (शनैः शनैः चर्वणम्) and drink clean water; (3) eat at regular, fixed times (समये भोजनम्) and never over undigested food (अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम्).
questions.explanation: Moderation plus freshness, slow chewing, clean water and regular timing.

questions.question: Explain the maxim अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम्. Why is such eating compared to poison?
questions.answer: The maxim means: when the earlier meal is still undigested (अजीर्णे — locative of condition), eating another meal is like poison (विषम्). It is compared to poison because food taken over an unfinished digestion is not properly digested; instead of nourishing the body it burdens and harms it, causing heaviness and disease — like a toxin rather than a food.
questions.explanation: The locative अजीर्णे states the condition; food without digestion harms instead of nourishing.

questions.question: Explain the description हितभुक् मितभुक् ऋतभुक् — what three qualities of the ideal eater does it name?
questions.answer: The phrase describes the disciplined eater by three qualities: (1) हितभुक् — he eats what is wholesome and beneficial (हित), not merely what is tasty; (2) मितभुक् — he eats in moderation (मित), in measured quantity; (3) ऋतभुक् — he eats what is honestly and righteously earned (ऋत). Together they teach that WHAT we eat, HOW MUCH we eat, and HOW the food was obtained all matter for true health.
questions.explanation: Wholesomeness, moderation and honest earning — the three marks of the ideal eater.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय of Gita 6.17 (युक्ताहारविहारस्य...) and translate it into English.
questions.answer:
अन्वय: युक्ताहारविहारस्य, कर्मसु युक्तचेष्टस्य, युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य (पुरुषस्य) योगः दुःखहा भवति।
Translation: For the person whose food and recreation are regulated, whose effort in actions is regulated, and whose sleep and waking are regulated, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
questions.explanation: Three genitive phrases qualify the implied पुरुषस्य; योगः दुःखहा भवति is the main clause.

questions.question: State any four benefits of regular व्यायाम mentioned in the lesson, using at least two Sanskrit expressions.
questions.answer: Regular exercise (1) makes the body firm — व्यायामेन शरीरं दृढं भवति; (2) strengthens the digestive power — जाठराग्निः वर्धते; (3) makes the mind cheerful — मनः प्रसन्नं भवति; (4) done regularly and moderately (walking, योगासन, outdoor क्रीडा), it keeps the whole दिनचर्या in rhythm — while excess even in exercise is to be avoided.
questions.explanation: Firm body, strong digestion, cheerful mind, regularity — with moderation.

questions.question: A friend studies till 2 a.m. daily and dozes in class. Using the lesson's teaching on निद्रा, what would you advise?
questions.answer: I would advise timely sleep and timely rising — समये शयनं समये उत्थानं च आरोग्यस्य रक्षकम्. Sleep repairs the body and refreshes memory and attention, so studying late into the night actually weakens learning. He should fix a regular bedtime, sleep sufficiently, rise early in the ब्राह्ममुहूर्त and study then — the morning mind is fresh and retains more, and Gita 6.17 reminds us that sleep and waking must both be युक्त (regulated).
questions.explanation: Apply the sleep rules: regular timing, sufficiency, early rising, regulated waking.

questions.question: Why is स्वच्छता called the basis of health? Give three practices of cleanliness from the lesson.
questions.answer: Much disease travels through unclean hands, water and surroundings, so cleanliness stops disease before it begins — स्वच्छता एव आरोग्यस्य आधारः. Three practices: (1) wash the hands before eating — भोजनात् पूर्वं हस्तौ प्रक्षालयेत्; (2) wear clean clothes and keep the home, school and surroundings clean (परिसरस्वच्छता); (3) keep food and water covered and drink clean water.
questions.explanation: Cleanliness as disease-prevention, with hand-washing, clean surroundings and covered food/water.

questions.question: What is ऋतुचर्या? Name the six ऋतुs and give one seasonal rule each for ग्रीष्म and वर्षा.
questions.answer: ऋतुचर्या (ऋतूनां चर्या) is the seasonal regimen — adjusting food, dress and habits to each season. The six ऋतुs are: वसन्तः (spring), ग्रीष्मः (summer), वर्षा (rains), शरद् (autumn), हेमन्तः (early winter), शिशिरः (late winter). In ग्रीष्म one should take plenty of water, light food and protection from the sun; in वर्षा one should drink boiled or clean water and eat freshly cooked food, since impure water spreads disease most in the rains.
questions.explanation: Definition, the six seasons, and the summer and monsoon rules.

questions.question: 'Live with the season, not against it.' Explain this principle of ऋतुचर्या with two contrasting examples from the lesson.
questions.answer: The principle means our food, dress and habits should cooperate with what each season does to the body, instead of ignoring it. Contrast 1: in ग्रीष्म the body loses water and digestion weakens, so the lesson prescribes plenty of water and light food — heavy fried food in summer works AGAINST the season. Contrast 2: in हेमन्त-शिशिर the digestive power is strong, so nourishing food and warm clothing suit the body — while eating too little or dressing thinly in winter fights the season. Health comes from adapting each season's regimen, not from one fixed routine all year.
questions.explanation: Seasonal adaptation: light food and water in summer versus nourishing food and warmth in winter.

questions.question: How do bodily health and mental health support each other? Give one example in each direction from the lesson.
questions.answer: The lesson says शरीरस्य मनसः च स्वास्थ्यम् उभयम् आवश्यकम् — both healths are necessary and each supports the other. Body helping mind: regular व्यायाम makes the mind cheerful (मनः प्रसन्नं भवति), and timely निद्रा refreshes memory and attention. Mind helping body: a calm, contented mind (सन्तोष, ध्यान, प्राणायाम) keeps anger and worry away, and a worried, angry mind disturbs sleep, appetite and digestion, weakening the body. So neglecting either side eventually damages both.
questions.explanation: Two-way support: exercise/sleep cheer the mind; calm contentment protects the body.

questions.question: Explain the four attitudes of चित्तप्रसादनम् (योगसूत्र 1.33), stating toward whom each is directed.
questions.answer: चित्तप्रसादनम् — the calming and clarifying of the mind — comes through four attitudes: (1) मैत्री, friendliness, directed toward the happy (सुख), so that envy does not arise; (2) करुणा, compassion, toward the suffering (दुःख), so that indifference or cruelty does not arise; (3) मुदिता, gladness, toward the virtuous (पुण्य), so that jealousy does not arise; (4) उपेक्षा, equanimity, toward the wrongdoer (अपुण्य), so that hatred and anger do not arise. Practising these four keeps the mind clear of its chief toxins.
questions.explanation: मैत्री/happy, करुणा/suffering, मुदिता/virtuous, उपेक्षा/wrongdoer — each blocks a mental toxin.

questions.question: A classmate feels anxious before examinations. Suggest three traditional practices from the lesson for मनःस्वास्थ्य, with their Sanskrit names.
questions.answer: (1) प्राणायामः — a few minutes of slow, regulated breathing settles the anxious mind; (2) ध्यानम् — sitting quietly each morning watching the breath builds steadiness; (3) नियमितः क्रमः and सत्सङ्गः — keeping a regular study-sleep routine and talking openly with good friends, family or teachers lightens worry (चिन्ता-वर्जनम्). Contentment (सन्तोषः) — doing one's best without constant comparison — also calms examination fear.
questions.explanation: Breath regulation, meditation, routine and good company applied to exam anxiety.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: भाग्यम्, उत्तमम्, जीवितस्य, खलु, वर्जयेत्.
questions.answer: भाग्यम् = fortune, blessing; उत्तमम् = best, foremost; जीवितस्य = of life; खलु = indeed, surely; वर्जयेत् = one should avoid.
questions.explanation: Core vocabulary from the chapter's verses.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय of the moderation verse (अतिदानाद् बलिर्बद्धो...) and translate it.
questions.answer:
अन्वय: अतिदानात् बलिः बद्धः; अतिमानात् हि सुयोधनः (विनष्टः); अतिलौल्यात् रावणः हतः; (अतः) सर्वत्र अति वर्जयेत्।
Translation: Through excessive giving Bali was bound; through excessive pride Suyodhana perished; through excessive greed Ravana was slain — therefore one should avoid excess in everything.
questions.explanation: Three ablatives of cause (अतिदानात्, अतिमानात्, अतिलौल्यात्) lead to the injunction वर्जयेत्.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of: (a) रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः (b) युक्ताहारः (c) नास्ति.
questions.answer: (a) रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः = रोगाः + तस्य + अपहर्तारः (विसर्ग-सन्धि in रोगाः + तस्य; दीर्घ-सन्धि अ + अ = आ in तस्य + अपहर्तारः). (b) युक्ताहारः = युक्त + आहारः (दीर्घ-सन्धि, अ + आ = आ). (c) नास्ति = न + अस्ति (दीर्घ-सन्धि, अ + अ = आ).
questions.explanation: Visarga and long-vowel sandhis from the chapter's verses.

questions.question: Identify the समास type of each, with a one-line विग्रह: (a) दिनचर्या (b) मिताहारः (c) युक्ताहारविहारस्य.
questions.answer: (a) दिनचर्या = दिनस्य चर्या — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः (genitive relation). (b) मिताहारः = मितः चासौ आहारः — कर्मधारयः (adjective + noun). (c) युक्ताहारविहारस्य = युक्तौ आहारविहारौ यस्य सः, तस्य — बहुव्रीहिः ('of one WHOSE food and recreation are regulated'; inside it, आहारविहारौ is a द्वन्द्व).
questions.explanation: Three different compound types drawn from the chapter's key words.

questions.question: 'Health is the true wealth of life.' Evaluate this statement in the light of the three verses on आरोग्य in the lesson (the traditional maxim, Charaka's verse and Kalidasa's pada), in about 12 sentences.
questions.answer: The statement is fully supported by the tradition presented in the lesson. The maxim आरोग्यं परमं भाग्यं स्वास्थ्यं सर्वार्थसाधनम् calls health the highest fortune and the instrument of all achievement: money, position and possessions can be enjoyed only through a healthy body and mind. Charaka's verse goes deeper — आरोग्यं धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् उत्तमं मूलम्: health is the root of the four aims of life. A tree with a rotten root bears no fruit; likewise a life without health can achieve neither duty, nor wealth, nor joy, nor liberation. He warns that diseases are अपहर्तारः — robbers of health, welfare and life — so guarding health is guarding everything. Kalidasa adds the moral dimension: शरीरमाद्यं खलु धर्मसाधनम् — the body is the first instrument of dharma. Caring for the body is therefore not self-indulgence but a duty owed to all our other duties. Wealth without health is like a locked treasure whose key is lost: the sick rich man envies the healthy labourer. Moreover, health, unlike money, cannot be borrowed or bought back easily once squandered; it is preserved only by daily discipline — दिनचर्या, मित-आहार, निद्रा, व्यायाम, स्वच्छता and a calm mind. Hence the wise call आरोग्य the first wealth and the highest happiness — आरोग्यं परमं सुखम्. The statement is therefore not a poetic exaggeration but a sober, practical truth.
questions.explanation: Evaluation citing all three verses: health as fortune, as root of the पुरुषार्थs, and as instrument of dharma.

questions.question: Describe an ideal दिनचर्या for a senior-secondary student from morning to night, based on the lesson. Then compose three simple Sanskrit sentences of your own about this routine, with English meanings.
questions.answer:
An ideal दिनचर्या: rise in the ब्राह्ममुहूर्त before sunrise; perform शौच and दन्तधावन; do light व्यायाम, योगासन or a brisk walk; bathe and offer प्रार्थना; study in the fresh morning hours with a calm mind (शान्तमनसा); take a moderate wholesome breakfast at a fixed time; attend school attentively; in the evening play outdoors (क्रीडाङ्गणे क्रीडा) for refreshment; revise lessons briefly; take a light timely dinner; avoid screens late at night; and sleep at a fixed hour (समये शयनम्) so that the next day begins fresh. Regularity — the same times daily — is the soul of दिनचर्या.
Three Sanskrit sentences: (1) छात्रः प्रातः उत्थाय व्यायामं करोति। — The student, having risen in the morning, does exercise. (2) सः समये मितं भोजनं भुङ्क्ते। — He eats moderate food at the proper time. (3) रात्रौ सः समये शयनं करोति। — At night he goes to sleep at the proper time.
questions.explanation: Full daily routine in order, plus three original simple sentences using chapter vocabulary.

questions.question: Write an essay on आहारसंयम (discipline in diet) covering: the principles of good आहार, the maxims अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम् and हितभुक् मितभुक् ऋतभुक्, Charaka's three pillars, and the lesson of the verse अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत्.
questions.answer: Discipline in diet is the first pillar of health. The lesson's principles of good आहार are: fresh, simple food; seasonal fruits and vegetables; slow, thorough chewing; clean water; eating at fixed times; and मितभोजनम् — stopping a little before fullness. The maxim अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम् warns that food eaten over an undigested meal acts like poison: it burdens digestion and breeds disease instead of strength. The ideal eater is described as हितभुक् मितभुक् ऋतभुक् — eating what is wholesome, eating moderately, and eating what is honestly earned — so diet-discipline covers the quality, the quantity and even the moral source of food. Charaka counts आहार among the three pillars (त्रयः उपस्तम्भाः) of health, together with स्वप्न (sleep) and ब्रह्मचर्य (disciplined living): the house of health stands on all three, and weakening one shakes the rest. Finally, the verse अतिदानाद् बलिर्बद्धो... अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत् teaches that excess destroyed even the great — Bali by excessive giving, Suyodhana by pride, Ravana by greed — so excess must be avoided everywhere, and first of all at the dining plate. Overeating even wholesome food breaks the rule of मितता. In short, eat fresh, eat clean, eat on time, eat less than the appetite demands, and earn the food honestly: this is आहारसंयम, and it guards आरोग्य better than any medicine taken after illness arrives.
questions.explanation: Essay integrating diet principles, both maxims, the three pillars and the moderation verse.

questions.question: Explain Bhagavad Gita 6.17 (युक्ताहारविहारस्य...) with its अन्वय and translation, and show in detail how a senior-secondary student can apply its four 'regulations' to daily life.
questions.answer: अन्वय: युक्ताहारविहारस्य, कर्मसु युक्तचेष्टस्य, युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य (पुरुषस्य) योगः दुःखहा भवति। Translation: For one whose food and recreation are regulated, whose effort in work is regulated, and whose sleep and waking are regulated, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow. The verse names four fields of regulation. (1) युक्त-आहार — regulated food: a student should eat moderate, wholesome meals at fixed times, neither skipping breakfast in a rush nor snacking endlessly at night. (2) युक्त-विहार — regulated recreation: games, walks and entertainment refresh the mind, but in measure; hours of screen-time are विहार in excess and dull the mind. (3) युक्त-चेष्टा कर्मसु — regulated effort in work: steady daily study is better than frantic all-night cramming followed by idleness; effort should be constant, not convulsive. (4) युक्त-स्वप्न-अवबोध — regulated sleep and waking: fixed bedtime, sufficient sleep and early rising keep memory and attention sharp. The word युक्त means balanced — neither too much nor too little — and दुःखहा promises that such balance itself destroys sorrow: most student misery (fatigue, anxiety, poor marks) grows from unregulated food, play, work or sleep. A simple timetable honouring all four regulations is thus the Gita's practical prescription for a happy, healthy student life.
questions.explanation: Anvaya, translation, and the four regulations each applied concretely to student routine.

questions.question: Write a note on स्वच्छता and ऋतुचर्या as the two shields of health, describing the practices of cleanliness and the regimen for at least four of the six seasons.
questions.answer: स्वच्छता and ऋतुचर्या shield health from the two great sources of disease — impurity and seasonal stress. Cleanliness works daily: washing the hands before every meal (भोजनात् पूर्वं हस्तौ प्रक्षालयेत्), bathing, wearing clean clothes, keeping the home, school and surroundings clean, and keeping food and water covered. Since much disease travels through unclean hands, water and surroundings, स्वच्छता is prevention practised in small acts — स्वच्छता एव आरोग्यस्य आधारः. ऋतुचर्या adapts life to the six seasons (षड् ऋतवः). In ग्रीष्म (summer): plenty of water, light easily-digested food, and protection from the harsh sun. In वर्षा (rains): boiled or clean water and freshly cooked food, for impure water spreads disease most now; damp clothes and stale food are to be avoided. In शरद् (autumn): light, cooling food as the body recovers from the rains. In हेमन्त and शिशिर (winter): nourishing food — for the digestive fire is strongest — together with warm clothing and regular exercise. In वसन्त (spring): light food and active exercise as the body sheds winter heaviness. The principle throughout is to live WITH the season, not against it. Together, daily cleanliness and seasonal adjustment prevent most illness before any medicine is needed.
questions.explanation: Cleanliness practices plus season-wise regimen for summer, rains, autumn, winter and spring.

questions.question: 'मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः' — write an essay on मनःस्वास्थ्य in the light of this line, covering the mind-body relation, the traditional means of mental health, and the four भावनाs of योगसूत्र 1.33.
questions.answer: The Upanishadic line declares that the mind alone is the cause of our bondage and our freedom: the same mind, untrained, binds us with anger, worry and craving, and, trained, releases us into calm and clarity. Mental health is therefore not a luxury but the inner half of आरोग्य. The lesson stresses that body and mind support each other — शरीरस्य मनसः च स्वास्थ्यम् उभयम् आवश्यकम्: exercise and timely sleep cheer and steady the mind, while a calm mind protects appetite, sleep and digestion; an anxious, angry mind disturbs them all. The traditional means of मनःस्वास्थ्य are: सन्तोष — contentment, ceasing constant comparison with others; ध्यान — sitting quietly in meditation each day; प्राणायाम — slow regulation of the breath, which directly settles the mind; सत्सङ्ग — the company of good people, including speaking openly with family and teachers when the mind is heavy; a regular routine; and deliberate क्रोध-चिन्ता-वर्जन — refusing to feed anger and needless worry. Yoga-sutra 1.33 completes the picture with four attitudes for चित्तप्रसादन: मैत्री, friendliness toward the happy, which dissolves envy; करुणा, compassion toward the suffering, which dissolves hardness; मुदिता, gladness at the virtuous, which dissolves jealousy; and उपेक्षा, equanimity toward the wrongdoer, which dissolves hatred. Practised together, these habits turn the mind from our jailer into our liberator — exactly as the line promises: the mind is the cause of both bondage and release.
questions.explanation: Mind as cause of bondage/freedom; mind-body reciprocity; six means; the four भावनाs.

questions.question: Explain any two verses of the chapter (other than Gita 6.17) with: the verse text, शब्दार्थ of key words, अन्वय, English translation and भाव (purport).
questions.answer:
Verse 1 (Charaka, Sutrasthana 1.15): धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् आरोग्यं मूलमुत्तमम् । रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः श्रेयसो जीवितस्य च ॥ शब्दार्थ: धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् = of the four aims of life; मूलम् = root; उत्तमम् = best; रोगाः = diseases; अपहर्तारः = robbers; श्रेयसः = of welfare; जीवितस्य = of life. अन्वय: आरोग्यं धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् उत्तमं मूलम् (अस्ति); रोगाः तस्य श्रेयसः जीवितस्य च अपहर्तारः (भवन्ति)। Translation: Health is the best root of duty, wealth, desire and liberation; diseases are the robbers of that health, of welfare and of life. भाव: all human aims stand on health; disease steals everything valuable.
Verse 2 (moderation verse): अतिदानाद् बलिर्बद्धो ह्यतिमानात् सुयोधनः । अतिलौल्याद् रावणो हतः अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत् ॥ शब्दार्थ: अतिदानात् = from excessive giving; बद्धः = bound; अतिमानात् = from excessive pride; अतिलौल्यात् = from excessive greed; हतः = slain; वर्जयेत् = one should avoid. अन्वय: अतिदानात् बलिः बद्धः, अतिमानात् सुयोधनः (विनष्टः), अतिलौल्यात् रावणः हतः — सर्वत्र अति वर्जयेत्। Translation: Through excess of giving Bali was bound, through excess of pride Suyodhana perished, through excess of greed Ravana was slain — avoid excess everywhere. भाव: even virtues ruin when unmeasured; moderation in food, sleep, work and play is the key to आरोग्य.
questions.explanation: Two full verse expositions: text, word meanings, prose order, translation and purport.

questions.question: From the vocabulary of this chapter, explain with two examples each: (a) सन्धि and सन्धि-विच्छेद, (b) समास identification, (c) विभक्ति roles, (d) कृदन्त forms.
questions.answer:
(a) सन्धि: sounds merge where words meet. Examples: सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः (गुण-सन्धि, अ + उ = ओ); मूलम् + उत्तमम् = मूलमुत्तमम्. The reverse splitting is सन्धि-विच्छेद: रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः = रोगाः + तस्य + अपहर्तारः; नास्ति = न + अस्ति (दीर्घ-सन्धि).
(b) समास: दिनचर्या = दिनस्य चर्या — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष (genitive relation); धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् = धर्मश्च अर्थश्च कामश्च मोक्षश्च — द्वन्द्व (coordination); also मिताहारः (कर्मधारय) and युक्ताहारविहारस्य (बहुव्रीहि).
(c) विभक्ति: आरोग्येण — तृतीया, 'BY health'; अजीर्णे — सप्तमी, 'WHEN (food is) undigested' (locative of condition); also रोगात् (पञ्चमी, 'from disease') and आरोग्याय (चतुर्थी, 'for health').
(d) कृदन्त: स्नात्वा (स्ना + क्त्वा, 'having bathed') and भुक्त्वा (भुज् + क्त्वा, 'having eaten') — absolutives; रक्षितुम् (रक्ष् + तुमुन्, 'in order to protect') — infinitive of purpose; युक्तः and जीर्णम् (क्त participles, 'regulated', 'digested'); उत्थाय (उद्-स्था + ल्यप्, 'having risen').
questions.explanation: Two (or more) chapter-based examples for each of the four grammar devices.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'सुरेशः धनिकः अस्ति, परन्तु सः सर्वदा रुग्णः भवति। सः औषधानि खादति, किन्तु दिनचर्यां न पालयति। सः चिन्तयति — मम धनं किमर्थम्, यदि आरोग्यं नास्ति?'
(a) What has Suresh realised about wealth and health? (b) Which verse of Charaka explains his situation? (c) What does the phrase आरोग्यं नास्ति illustrate grammatically (सन्धि)?
questions.answer: (a) Suresh has realised that wealth without health is useless — he is rich (धनिकः) but always ill (रुग्णः), so his money cannot give him happiness; health, not wealth, is the true foundation of enjoyment. (b) Charaka's verse धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् आरोग्यं मूलमुत्तमम् — health is the best root of all four aims of life, and रोगाः are the robbers (अपहर्तारः) of welfare — explains why his wealth is fruitless while disease persists; medicines alone cannot replace a disciplined दिनचर्या. (c) नास्ति = न + अस्ति, a दीर्घ-सन्धि (अ + अ = आ).
questions.explanation: Wealth cannot substitute for health; Charaka's root-verse; नास्ति as दीर्घ-सन्धि.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'मीरा प्रातः पञ्चवादने उत्तिष्ठति। सा दन्तधावनं कृत्वा योगासनं करोति। स्नात्वा सा प्रार्थनां करोति, ततः एकां होरां पठति। सा समये विद्यालयं गच्छति।'
(a) List, in order, the five actions of Meera's morning. (b) Which two कृदन्त forms occur in the passage, and what do they mean? (c) How does Meera's routine match the lesson's दिनचर्या?
questions.answer: (a) In order: (1) she rises at five o'clock (उत्तिष्ठति); (2) cleans her teeth (दन्तधावनं कृत्वा); (3) does yoga postures (योगासनं करोति); (4) bathes and prays (स्नात्वा प्रार्थनां करोति); (5) studies for an hour and goes to school on time. (b) कृत्वा (कृ + क्त्वा) = 'having done', and स्नात्वा (स्ना + क्त्वा) = 'having bathed' — both absolutives showing completed prior actions. (c) Her routine matches the lesson's ideal दिनचर्या exactly: early rising, cleanliness, exercise, bath, prayer, morning study and punctuality (समये) — the rhythm that keeps body and mind fresh.
questions.explanation: Sequencing the routine, spotting the two क्त्वा forms, and mapping onto the ideal दिनचर्या.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'राजू विद्यालयस्य समीपे सर्वदा कुरकुरितानि भोज्यानि क्रीणाति। सः शीघ्रं शीघ्रं खादति, जलं च न पिबति। भोजनकाले अपि सः पुनः खादति। अधुना तस्य उदरे वेदना भवति।'
(a) Which three rules of आहार is Raju breaking? (b) Which maxim of the lesson fits his eating over an unfinished digestion? (c) Advise him in two points using the lesson's terms.
questions.answer: (a) Raju breaks: (1) the rule of fresh, wholesome food — he buys packaged fried snacks daily instead of हितं भोजनम्; (2) the rule of slow chewing and clean water — he eats hurriedly (शीघ्रं शीघ्रम्) and drinks no water; (3) the rule of मितभोजनम् and timing — he eats again at mealtime over the earlier snacks. (b) The maxim अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम् — eating while the earlier food is undigested is poison — explains his stomach-ache (उदरे वेदना). (c) Advice: eat मितं हितं च भोजनम् at fixed times only (समये भोजनम्), chewing slowly; and follow हितभुक् मितभुक् — choose wholesome food in moderate quantity, leaving proper gaps between meals.
questions.explanation: Applying the diet rules and अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम् to a snacking habit.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'कविता क्रीडायां तु उत्तमा, किन्तु सा प्रतिदिनं पञ्च होराः क्रीडति, रात्रौ च विलम्बेन पठति। परीक्षायां तस्याः अङ्काः न्यूनाः जाताः। सा खिन्ना अस्ति।'
(a) Kavita exercises a lot — why is she still failing by Gita 6.17's standard? (b) Which word of the verse names what her play lacks? (c) Rearrange her day using the verse's four regulations.
questions.answer: (a) Gita 6.17 requires balance in ALL fields — food, recreation, work, sleep and waking. Kavita's recreation (विहार) is excessive: five hours of daily play push study to late night, so her sleep and her effort in work (चेष्टा कर्मसु) are both unregulated. Excess in even a good thing (exercise/play) breaks the verse's standard — अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत्. (b) The word युक्त — 'regulated, measured' — is exactly what her play lacks; hers is play अयुक्त, unmeasured. (c) Rearranged day: moderate play of about an hour in the evening (युक्त-विहार); fixed study hours in the morning and afternoon with steady effort (कर्मसु युक्त-चेष्टा); meals at fixed times (युक्त-आहार); and a fixed early bedtime with early rising (युक्त-स्वप्न-अवबोध). With balance restored, both her marks and her mood should recover — योगो भवति दुःखहा.
questions.explanation: Excess recreation violates युक्त-विहार; the remedy is rebalancing all four regulations.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'वर्षाकाले ग्रामे बहवः जनाः रुग्णाः अभवन्। ते अशुद्धं जलम् अपिबन्, मार्गेषु च अवकरः आसीत्। बालकाः अप्रक्षालितैः हस्तैः भोजनम् अखादन्।'
(a) Identify the three causes of illness in the village. (b) Which season makes these lapses most dangerous, and why? (c) Give three corrective measures from the lesson, with Sanskrit terms.
questions.answer: (a) Three causes: (1) drinking impure water (अशुद्धं जलम्); (2) garbage lying on the roads (अवकरः) — unclean surroundings; (3) children eating with unwashed hands (अप्रक्षालितैः हस्तैः). (b) The rainy season (वर्षा) makes these most dangerous, because impure water spreads disease fastest in the rains — the lesson's ऋतुचर्या therefore singles out water discipline in वर्षा. (c) Corrective measures: drink boiled or clean water (शुद्धं जलम्); wash hands before every meal (भोजनात् पूर्वं हस्तौ प्रक्षालयेत्); and keep the surroundings clean (परिसरस्वच्छता) with food and water covered — स्वच्छता एव आरोग्यस्य आधारः.
questions.explanation: Monsoon hygiene case: unclean water, surroundings and hands, corrected by the lesson's rules.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'अनिलः परीक्षाफलात् पूर्वं रात्रौ न शेते, भोजनं च त्यजति। सः मित्रस्य उत्तमैः अङ्कैः ईर्ष्यां करोति, आत्मानं च निन्दति। तस्य शिरोवेदना अपि भवति।'
(a) How does Anil's mental state harm his body? (b) Which of the four भावनाs of योगसूत्र 1.33 is the antidote to his envy, and how? (c) Suggest two further practices from the lesson for his मनःस्वास्थ्य.
questions.answer: (a) His anxiety and self-blame disturb sleep (रात्रौ न शेते) and appetite (भोजनं त्यजति) and produce headache (शिरोवेदना) — showing the lesson's point that mind and body support or damage each other: an unquiet mind breaks the body's rhythm. (b) मुदिता — gladness at another's merit — is the antidote to his envy (ईर्ष्या) of his friend's marks: by training himself to feel genuine joy at the friend's success, the burning of comparison subsides; सन्तोष (contentment with one's own sincere effort) completes the cure. (c) Two further practices: प्राणायाम and ध्यान — slow regulated breathing and quiet sitting to settle the mind — and सत्सङ्ग with open conversation: speaking honestly with family, teachers or good friends instead of निन्दा of himself, along with a regular routine of समये भोजनं शयनं च.
questions.explanation: Mind-body damage loop; मुदिता against envy; breath, meditation, good company and routine.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
'धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणाम् आरोग्यं मूलमुत्तमम् ।
रोगास्तस्यापहर्तारः श्रेयसो जीवितस्य च ॥'
(a) Give the शब्दार्थ of मूलम्, अपहर्तारः and श्रेयसः. (b) Write the अन्वय of the second line. (c) In one sentence, state the भाव (purport) of the verse.
questions.answer: (a) मूलम् = root, foundation; अपहर्तारः = takers-away, robbers; श्रेयसः = of welfare, of the good. (b) अन्वय of the second line: रोगाः तस्य (आरोग्यस्य), श्रेयसः जीवितस्य च अपहर्तारः (भवन्ति) — diseases are the robbers of that health, of welfare and of life. (c) भाव: since health is the root on which all four aims of life stand, and disease robs us of health, welfare and life itself, guarding आरोग्य is the first duty of anyone who wishes to achieve anything.
questions.explanation: Word meanings, prose order of line two, and the verse's purport.

questions.question:
Read the sentence and answer:
'छात्रः सूर्योदयात् पूर्वम् उत्थाय, स्नात्वा, शरीरं रक्षितुं व्यायामं करोति।'
(a) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of सूर्योदयात् and name the सन्धि. (b) Identify the कृदन्त suffix in each of: उत्थाय, स्नात्वा, रक्षितुम्. (c) State the विभक्ति of सूर्योदयात् and its meaning here.
questions.answer: (a) सूर्योदयात् = सूर्य + उदयात् — गुण-सन्धिः (अ + उ = ओ). (b) उत्थाय = उद्-स्था + ल्यप् ('having risen' — ल्यप् because the root has a prefix); स्नात्वा = स्ना + क्त्वा ('having bathed'); रक्षितुम् = रक्ष् + तुमुन् ('in order to protect'). (c) सूर्योदयात् is पञ्चमी (ablative), used with पूर्वम् to mean 'BEFORE sunrise' — the ablative marks the point from which 'before' is reckoned.
questions.explanation: Guna sandhi, three krt suffixes (ल्यप्, क्त्वा, तुमुन्), and the ablative with पूर्वम्.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'एकः छात्रः वदति — अहं बलवान् भवितुम् इच्छामि, अतः अहं प्रतिदिनं द्विगुणं भोजनं खादामि, होराद्वयं च व्यायामं करोमि। तथापि अहं श्रान्तः भवामि।'
(a) Why is the student's plan failing despite 'healthy' activities? (b) Which verse-teaching of the chapter corrects him? (c) Rewrite his plan in two balanced points.
questions.answer: (a) His plan fails because he has doubled quantity instead of improving quality and balance: double meals burden digestion (against मितभोजनम् — and risk अजीर्णे भोजनं विषम्), and two hours of heavy exercise without measure exhausts rather than strengthens. Health comes from regulation, not from 'more'. (b) The teaching अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत् — avoid excess in everything — corrects him: even good things (food, exercise) harm in excess; Gita 6.17 likewise demands युक्त (measured) आहार and चेष्टा. (c) Balanced plan: (1) eat मितं हितं च भोजनम् at fixed times — wholesome food in moderate quantity, well chewed; (2) do moderate daily व्यायाम (walking, योगासन, games) with timely निद्रा, increasing gradually — strength grows from steady moderation, not sudden excess.
questions.explanation: Excess of even good habits fails; moderation verses supply the correction.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'रात्रौ शयनात् पूर्वं रोहितः चलदूरवाण्यां चलच्चित्राणि पश्यति। तस्य मनः चञ्चलं भवति, निद्रा विलम्बेन आगच्छति, प्रातः च सः क्लान्तः उत्तिष्ठति। सः चिन्तयति — मम मनः शान्तं कथं भवेत्?'
(a) What is disturbing Rohit's mind and sleep? (b) Answer his question with three practices from the lesson, in Sanskrit terms with brief meaning. (c) Which Upanishadic line tells him that the remedy lies in his own mind?
questions.answer: (a) Watching videos on his phone just before bed agitates his mind (मनः चञ्चलम्), delays sleep and leaves him tired at rising — unregulated late-night विहार breaking the rule of समये शयनम्. (b) Three practices: (1) ध्यानम् — sit quietly for a few minutes watching the breath before bed instead of the screen; (2) प्राणायामः — slow regulated breathing to settle the restless mind; (3) नियमितः क्रमः / समये शयनम् — a fixed screen-free hour before a fixed bedtime; सन्तोषः and light reading or प्रार्थना may replace the videos. (c) The line मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः — the mind alone causes bondage and freedom — tells him the disturbance and its remedy both lie in his own mind, which can be trained.
questions.explanation: Late-night screens as unregulated विहार; meditation, breath and routine as remedies.
